decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY selecting Option B, defining the reach and terminal variants, applying them consistently across all three glyphs, and reopening the terminal study.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY that records the extremely subtle Hero V right-arm reach study, preserved slope and geometry, and limited reopening of the asset.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the parallel second-V reach increase while preserving its established slope and overall geometry.
The client limits the requested refinements to the Hero V, second V, and É accent and asks to keep everything else unchanged; the E and L requirements remain valid without modification.
Applying the same subtle reach refinement to both the Hero V and É accent does not change the requirement that their highest points align exactly.
The source changes glyph reach and terminal nuances only and explicitly preserves everything else; it does not alter the selected Satin Reflection finish or gold distribution.
The subtle right-arm reach study does not necessarily change the second V's established scale, left-arm cap-height relationship, or relative hierarchy within the wordmark.
The refinements start from the selected Option B Balanced Flow composition and keep everything else unchanged, so the established kerning state remains valid.
The source requests visual refinement variants but does not change the obligation to explain design intentions with review rounds.
The source does not request any E or L scaling change and explicitly keeps the surrounding architecture unchanged.
Extending the right arms at their upper terminals does not change the established common baseline alignment of the glyph bottoms.
The source contains no decision about proof attachment formats or Mac viewability.
